mainTopic: The רביעה שניה and its halachic uses, the meaning and measure of רביעה, when rain shows the curse of ״וְעָצַר״ is absent, and the ברכה on rain.
overview: The גמרא lists practical halachos that depend on the date of the רביעה שניה, the second rainfall of the season. They are: a vow 'until the rains,' when anyone may take olives left for the poor (רב זביד), walking on שבילי הרשות (רב פפא), and the deadline for ביעור of פירות שביעית (רב נחמן בר יצחק), which is learned from a פסוק. Along the way it defines the rare word נמושות, with two views from רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. Next, רבי אבהו explains that רביעה means rain that fertilizes the earth, the earth's 'husband.' He also gives the amount of rain needed for the first and second רביעה. רב חסדא then teaches when rain shows that the curse of ״וְעָצַר״ is not happening, and אביי limits his rule about morning rain. The גמרא settles apparent contradictions about morning clouds, rain in טבת, and rain falling on only part of the country. Finally, רבי אבהו says when we bless over rain, and רב and רבי יוחנן give the words of the ברכה. רבא fixes its ending to ״אל ההודאות״, and רב פפא begins a practical ruling that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A vow 'until the rains' lasts until the second rainfall
steps.stepSummary: A source shows that the רביעה שניה matters for נדרים. Someone who vows 'until the rains' stays bound until the second rainfall falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who vows 'until the rains': the vow lasts from when the rains start falling until the second rainfall comes down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of explaining why the date of the רביעה שניה matters. Here it quotes a source showing that it matters for vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person said 'I won't have this benefit until the rains.' But the rainy season is a stretch of time, not a single day. This source says the 'time of rains' runs until the רביעה שניה, so that is when the vow ends.

keyTerms.meaning: Until the rains: the wording of the vow
The second rainfall of the rainy season

phrases.english: One who vows 'until the rains':
from when the rains fall
phrases.notes: The vow is in effect from the start of the rains.

phrases.english: until the second rainfall falls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) about why the date of the רביעה שניה matters.
steps.raayaObject: The date of the רביעה שניה has practical meaning for vows.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source on נדרים: הנודר עד הגשמים

steps.title: רב זביד: the second rainfall matters for olives
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד gives another practical difference: the date of the רביעה שניה matters for olives.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said: it matters for olives.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד adds a second practical use for the date of the רביעה שניה: olives. He is setting up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement here is only a heading. The proof that follows explains what about olives depends on this date: when ordinary people may take olives that were left for the poor.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the olives answer

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said: for olives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different practical difference for the רביעה שניה, after the one about vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The date of the רביעה שניה matters for the law of olives.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: when anyone may take the poor's produce
steps.stepSummary: A משנה lists when anyone may take produce set aside for the poor. For olives, the cutoff is the רביעה שניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: From when may anyone take לקט, שכחה, and פאה? From when the נמושות have gone. פרט and עוללות? From when the poor have gone through the vineyard and come back. Olives? From when the second rainfall falls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to prove רב זביד's point. For olives, ordinary people may take what was left for the poor once the רביעה שניה has fallen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gifts for the poor belong only to the poor until it is clear the poor have given up on them. For grain and grapes, the sign is that the last poor people have passed through. For olives, the sign is the רביעה שניה, so this date has a real halachic effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Stalks that fall during harvest, left for the poor
Sheaves forgotten in the field, left for the poor
The corner of the field, left for the poor
Single grapes that fall during harvest
Small, poorly formed grape clusters, left for the poor
The last group of poor gleaners (defined in the next step)

steps.confusionAlert: 'מותרין כל אדם' does not mean the poor lose their rights early. It means that only after the poor are finished may anyone, even a rich person, take what is left.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
From when is anyone permitted
in gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and pe'a?
From when the namoshot have gone.
In single grapes and small clusters:
from when the poor have gone into the vineyard and come back.
In olives:
from when the second rainfall falls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב זביד's statement with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The date of the רביעה שניה matters for olives.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה listing when anyone may take לקט, שכחה, פאה, פרט, עוללות, and olives.

steps.title: What does the word נמושות mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops briefly to ask what the rare word נמושות in the משנה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are נמושות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes a short side-trip to define a hard word from the משנה it just quoted. This sets up two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question about a word, not an attack. The answer will tell us exactly which group of poor people must finish before everyone else may take the produce.

phrases.english: What are 'namoshot'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about a word in the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word נמושות.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: old people who walk with a cane
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says נמושות are old people who walk with a cane.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: old people who walk with a cane.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. נמושות are elderly poor people leaning on canes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Old people walk very slowly, so they see and collect everything they want. Once even they have passed through, the poor are clearly done, and anyone may take what is left.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
old people who walk with a cane.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: סָבֵי דְּאָזְלִי אַתִּיגְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נמושות are elderly people who walk slowly with canes.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the gleaners who come after the gleaners
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says נמושות are the second round of gleaners, who come after the first gleaners.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: gleaners after gleaners.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different definition. נמושות are the late gleaners who pass through after the first group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the sign that the poor are done is the slowest walkers. For ריש לקיש, it is the second round of gleaners. Either way, the idea is the same: once the last group has passed, everyone may take.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who often disagrees with רבי יוחנן

steps.whatToRemember: There are two definitions of נמושות. רבי יוחנן says slow elderly people with canes. ריש לקיש says the second round of gleaners.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
gleaners after gleaners.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לָקוֹטֵי בָּתַר לָקוֹטֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 4 that differs from רבי יוחנן's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: נמושות are the second wave of gleaners.

steps.title: רב פפא: the second rainfall matters for walking on public paths
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives a third practical difference: the date of the רביעה שניה decides until when people may walk on שבילי הרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: it matters for knowing until when one may walk on the permitted paths.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to its main list. רב פפא says the רביעה שניה matters for walking on paths through private fields.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually people may cut across private fields on certain paths, because doing so causes no damage. רב פפא says the date of the רביעה שניה marks when this permission ends.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives the third answer
Paths through private fields that the public may use

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
for walking on the permitted paths.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: כְּדֵי לְהַלֵּךְ בִּשְׁבִילֵי הָרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side-trip about נמושות, goes back to listing practical differences of the רביעה שניה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The date of the רביעה שניה decides until when people may use paths through private fields.

steps.title: Proof: people may walk on the paths until the second rainfall
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב פפא: anyone may walk on שבילי הרשות until the רביעה שניה falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Master said: anyone may walk on the permitted paths until the second rainfall falls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב פפא with a teaching: walking on these paths is allowed only until the רביעה שניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the second rainfall, the fields are plowed and sown. Walking on them then would trample the crops and damage the owner's field, so the permission ends at that date.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (introduces a known teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: So far the רביעה שניה matters in three ways: when a vow 'until the rains' ends, when anyone may take olives left for the poor (רב זביד), and when walking on שבילי הרשות stops being allowed (רב פפא). The next step adds a fourth: the deadline for ביעור of פירות שביעית (רב נחמן בר יצחק).

phrases.english: As the Master said:
anyone may walk on the permitted paths
until the second rainfall falls.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: מְהַלְּכִין כׇּל אָדָם בִּשְׁבִילֵי הָרְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's statement from step 7 with a source.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that the רביעה שניה ends the right to walk on שבילי הרשות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא introduced with דאמר מר.

steps.title: A fourth use: the deadline for removing שביעית produce
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the date of the רביעה שניה also sets the deadline for ביעור of פירות שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the second rainfall matters for knowing when to remove פירות שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds another item to the list of practical uses for the רביעה שניה (after vows, רב זביד's olives, and רב פפא's paths): the time of the רביעה שניה tells us when פירות שביעית must be removed from the house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רב פפא said the רביעה שניה decides until when people may walk on שבילי הרשות. Now רב נחמן בר יצחק adds a different area of halacha that uses the same date: ביעור, the removal of שביעית produce. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove or get rid of (ביעור): taking שביעית produce out of one's possession once its time is over
Produce that grew during the Sabbatical (seventh) year, which has special holiness and rules

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
[It matters for knowing when] to remove the produce of the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: This continues the list of practical uses for the date of the second rainfall.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: לְבַעֵר פֵּירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth practical difference after רב פפא's third one (שבילי הרשות).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רביעה שניה marks the deadline for ביעור of פירות שביעית.

steps.title: A משנה proves the deadline is the second rainfall
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that one may use and burn שביעית straw and hay until the רביעה שניה falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Until when may one benefit from and burn straw and hay of שביעית? Until the second rainfall falls.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove רב נחמן בר יצחק's claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that straw and hay of שביעית may be used only until the רביעה שניה. After that, their time is over. So the date of the רביעה שניה really does set a halachic deadline for שביעית produce.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (in a משנה), used to bring a proof from a משנה
Straw and hay (stubble), plant leftovers used as animal food or fuel

phrases.english: As we learned: until when may one benefit
and burn straw and hay of the Sabbatical Year?
phrases.notes: Burning them for fuel counts as using them.

phrases.english: Until the second rainfall falls.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: עַד מָתַי נֶהֱנִין וְשׂוֹרְפִין בְּתֶבֶן וּבְקַשׁ שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב נחמן בר יצחק's statement with a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the רביעה שניה is the deadline for using and removing שביעית produce.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה (מסכת שביעית) about straw and hay of שביעית.

steps.title: Why must שביעית produce be removed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind ביעור of שביעית produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: where does the rule of removing שביעית produce come from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know from the משנה that there is a deadline. Now the גמרא wants the source in the תורה that explains why such a deadline exists at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? Asking for the source or logic of a rule

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the biblical basis of the rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the obligation to remove שביעית produce once its time is over.

steps.title: The פסוק: when food is gone for wild animals, remove it from your house
steps.stepSummary: From ״וְלִבְהֶמְתְּךָ וְלַחַיָּה אֲשֶׁר בְּאַרְצֶךָ״ we learn that once a food is gone from the field for wild animals, you must stop feeding it to your animals at home.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: ״And for your cattle and for the wild animals in your land.״ As long as the wild animal can eat in the field, you may feed your cattle at home. Once it is gone for the wild animal from the field, remove it for your cattle from the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק: you may keep שביעית food at home only as long as that same food is still available to wild animals in the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts your animals and the wild animals side by side. So the rule is: same access for both. After the רביעה שניה, the rain ruins the straw and hay in the fields, so wild animals no longer have it. That is when you must remove it from your house too.

keyTerms.meaning: Your domestic animal (cattle kept at home)
A wild animal that eats in the field

steps.whatToRemember: The ביעור deadline for each kind of שביעית produce is when that food is no longer found in the field. For straw and hay, that is the רביעה שניה.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And for your cattle
and for the wild animals in your land."
As long as the wild animal eats in the field,
feed your cattle in the house.
Once it is gone for the wild animal from the field,
remove it for your cattle from the house.
phrases.notes: Note the wordplay: כָּלָה (it is finished) and כַּלֵּה (finish it off).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מאי טעמא question with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links home use to field availability. When a food is gone from the field, it must be removed from the house.

steps.title: What the word רביעה means
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that רביעה means something that makes the ground fertile.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: What is the meaning of the word ״רביעה״? Something that makes the ground fertile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns from the list of uses to rain itself. רבי אבהו explains why rainfall is called רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word רביעה comes from רובע, which is used for an animal mating. So rain is called רביעה because it fertilizes the ground and makes it produce, like a husband with his wife. The next step backs this up.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording or term, its language meaning
Fertilizes, makes fruitful (the root of the word רביעה)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read רביעה as 'a quarter' (רביע). Here it comes from the word for fertilizing.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
What is the meaning of the word "revia"?
Something that fertilizes the ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the list of practical uses and starts a new topic: the meaning of the word רביעה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רביעה means rain that fertilizes the ground.

steps.title: רב יהודה: rain is the husband of the earth
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו's explanation matches רב יהודה, who says rain is the earth's husband and proves it from a פסוק in ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches רב יהודה, for רב יהודה said: Rain is the husband of the earth, as it says: ״For as the rain comes down and the snow from heaven, and does not return there unless it has watered the earth and made it give birth and sprout.״
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי אבהו's explanation fits a statement of רב יהודה, which is based on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the rain makes the earth ״give birth״ (וְהוֹלִידָהּ), which is language used for a husband and wife. So rain is pictured as the earth's husband. This supports reading רביעה as 'fertilizing'.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with the view of רב יהודה

phrases.english: In line with Rav Yehuda, for Rav Yehuda said:
Rain is the husband of the earth,
as it is said: "For as the rain comes down
and the snow from heaven,
and does not return there
unless it has watered the earth
and made it give birth and sprout."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו נה:י. The word 'give birth' is the key proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מִיטְרָא בַּעְלַהּ דְּאַרְעָא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's explanation of the word רביעה.
steps.raayaObject: That rain is called רביעה because it fertilizes the earth.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's statement, based on ישעיהו נה:י.

steps.title: How much rain counts as the first and second רביעה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו gives the amounts: the first רביעה soaks one טפח into the ground; the second makes enough mud to seal the opening of a barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: The first rainfall is enough to soak one handbreadth into the ground. The second is enough to seal the opening of a barrel with it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a measure for each רביעה, so we know when a rainfall really counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every drizzle counts as a רביעה. The first must soak a טפח deep. The second must wet the earth enough that its mud can seal a barrel's opening. This tells us exactly when the halachos from earlier, which depend on the רביעה שניה, take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The first rainfall of the season

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.aramaic: רְבִיעָה רִאשׁוֹנָה — כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּרֵד בַּקַּרְקַע טֶפַח.
phrases.english: The first rainfall: enough that it goes down into the ground one handbreadth.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנִיָּה — כְּדֵי לָגוּף בָּהּ פִּי חָבִית.
phrases.english: The second: enough to seal the opening of a barrel with it.
phrases.notes: Meaning the soil becomes muddy enough to plug a barrel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second statement of רבי אבהו, moving from the word's meaning to its required amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First רביעה: soaks one טפח. Second רביעה: enough mud to seal a barrel's opening.

steps.title: Enough rain to seal a barrel means no curse of drought
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says that if rain fell enough to seal a barrel's opening, the year is not under the curse of ״וְעָצַר״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Rains that fell enough to seal the opening of a barrel with them do not count as ״And He will close up [the heavens]״.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא uses the same barrel measure to say when a year is not considered a year of drought-curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה warns ״וְעָצַר אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם״, that ה׳ will hold back the rain. רב חסדא says that if enough rain fell to seal a barrel, that curse has not happened. This links the halachic measure of rain to the question of blessing and curse.

keyTerms.meaning: "And He will close up" (דברים יא:יז): the curse that the heavens will be shut and there will be no rain
They do not fall under the category of

steps.whatToRemember: The 'barrel-sealing' amount of rain is both the measure of the רביעה שניה and the sign that the year is not under the curse of ״וְעָצַר״.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
Rains that fell
enough to seal the opening of a barrel with them
do not count as "And He will close up."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: גְּשָׁמִים שֶׁיָּרְדוּ כְּדֵי לָגוּף בָּהֶן פִּי חָבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אבהו's barrel measure for a new purpose: deciding when the curse of ״וְעָצַר״ has not happened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain enough to seal a barrel's opening means the year is not a fulfillment of ״וְעָצַר״.

steps.title: Rain before saying "וְעָצַר" cancels the curse
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that rain falling before the words "וְעָצַר" are said in קריאת שמע means the curse of "וְעָצַר" does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: Rain that fell before "and He will close up" does not count as "and He will close up."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רב חסדא about rain. If rain falls before a person says the words "וְעָצַר" in קריאת שמע, that day is not under the curse of closed-up heavens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second paragraph of קריאת שמע warns that ה׳ will "close up the heavens" (וְעָצַר אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם). רב חסדא says that if rain already came before we reach those words, the warning is not being fulfilled at that time. This builds on his earlier statement in Step 16 about rain that seals a barrel.

keyTerms.meaning: "And He will close up [the heavens]", from the second paragraph of קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
They do not fall under the category of

steps.confusionAlert: Here "וְעָצַר" does not just mean the curse in general. It refers to the moment you say those words in קריאת שמע, which is used as a time marker.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
Rain that fell before "and He will close up"
phrases.notes: Before reciting this phrase in קריאת שמע

phrases.english: does not fall under "and He will close up."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רב חסדא on the same theme of "וְעָצַר"
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain that falls before one recites "וְעָצַר" in קריאת שמע shows the day is not under that curse.

steps.title: אביי limits this to the evening קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: אביי says רב חסדא's rule applies only to rain before the evening "וְעָצַר". Rain before the morning "וְעָצַר" can still be part of the curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: We only said this about before the evening "and He will close up." But before the morning "and He will close up", it can still count as "and He will close up."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows רב חסדא's rule. Rain during the day, before the evening קריאת שמע, cancels the curse. A little rain in the early morning does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two times we say "וְעָצַר": in the morning and in the evening. אביי says only rain that came before the evening recitation counts. A small morning rain could still be followed by a dry day. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said [this] in the case of; a formula that limits a rule

phrases.english: Abaye said:
We only said this
before the "and He will close up" of the evening
but before the "and He will close up" of the morning
it does count as "and He will close up."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of רב חסדא's rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only rain before the evening "וְעָצַר" cancels the curse. Rain before the morning "וְעָצַר" does not.

steps.title: Morning clouds have no substance
steps.stepSummary: אביי's reasoning is supported by רב יהודה בר יצחק, who says morning clouds bring little rain, based on a פסוק in הושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה בר יצחק said: These morning clouds have no substance, as it is written: "What can I do for you, אפרים? What can I do for you, יהודה? Your kindness is like a morning cloud..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason behind אביי's limit. Morning clouds usually bring little or no real rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares weak, short-lived kindness to a morning cloud that quickly disappears. This shows morning clouds are not reliable, so morning rain does not prove the day is blessed with rain.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda bar Yitzchak said:
These morning clouds
have no substance,
as it is written: "What can I do for you, Ephraim,
what can I do for you, Judah,
for your kindness is like a morning cloud, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's limit with a teaching and a פסוק
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that morning rain does not cancel "וְעָצַר"
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה בר יצחק, based on הושע ו:ד

steps.title: A popular saying: morning rain means rain all day
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי with a common saying that rain at the opening of the gates in the morning means the donkey-driver should go back to sleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: But people say: "When the gates open and there is rain, donkey-driver, fold your sack and go to sleep!"
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes back on אביי. People commonly say that rain in the early morning means it will rain all day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donkey-driver cannot work in heavy rain. The saying tells him to go back to bed if it rains in the morning, because the rain will last all day. This contradicts the idea that morning clouds bring little rain.

keyTerms.meaning: People say; introduces a popular saying
Fold your sack and go to sleep

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But people say:
When the gates open and there is rain,
donkey-driver, fold your sack and go to sleep!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, וְהָא אָמְרִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's claim about morning clouds
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim (Steps 18-19) that morning clouds bring little rain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A common saying assumes morning rain lasts all day, which contradicts אביי.

steps.title: Heavy clouds versus light clouds
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the saying refers to a sky covered with thick clouds, while אביי refers to light clouds.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: This one is when the sky is covered with thick clouds, and that one is when it is covered with light clouds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction. Both are true, but they describe different kinds of morning clouds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick, heavy clouds in the morning bring a full day of rain, as the saying claims. Light morning clouds bring little rain, as אביי said. So אביי's limit stands for ordinary light morning clouds.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; introduces an answer that splits the cases

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is when it is covered with thick clouds,
that is when it is covered with light clouds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (different types of clouds)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All morning rain clouds behave the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: Thick morning clouds bring rain all day. Light morning clouds bring little rain.
steps.whatToRemember: Rain before the evening "וְעָצַר" cancels the curse. Morning rain usually does not, because light morning clouds bring little rain, unless the clouds are thick.

steps.title: A dry טבת is good for the year
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says a year is good when טבת is a "widow", meaning it has no rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It is good for the year when טבת is a widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new teaching. רב יהודה says it is a good sign when the month of טבת has no rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 14), rain was called the earth's husband. Calling טבת a "widow" means the land is without its "husband", the rain. רב יהודה says that is actually good for the year.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow; here meaning without rain

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
It is good for the year when Tevet is a widow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about rain and the seasons
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rainless טבת is a good sign for the year.

steps.title: Two reasons a dry טבת is good
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two explanations. Either gardens will not be ruined, or the crops will not suffer blight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: so that the gardens will not be ruined. And some say: so that it will not suffer blight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a dry טבת is good. Two different reasons are offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reason is that too much rain ruins vegetable gardens. The second is that too much rain causes blight in the grain. Both agree that extra rain in טבת can cause harm.

phrases.english: Some say:
so that the gardens will not be ruined;
and some say:
so that it will not suffer blight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for רב יהודה's statement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dry טבת is good either to protect gardens or to prevent blight.

steps.title: But רב חסדא says a muddy טבת is good
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה with רב חסדא's teaching that a muddy, rainy טבת is good for the year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב חסדא said: It is good for the year when טבת is muddy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. רב חסדא says the opposite: a rainy, muddy טבת is good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה praises a dry טבת and רב חסדא praises a wet one. Both cannot be true without some difference between the cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so?; introduces a challenge

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rav Chisda say:
It is good for the year when Tevet is muddy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה with a contradicting statement
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's statement that a dry טבת is good
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא says the opposite, that a rainy טבת is good.

steps.title: It depends on whether rain already fell before טבת
steps.stepSummary: The answer: if rain already fell before טבת, a dry טבת is better. If no rain fell earlier, a rainy טבת is better.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: This one is when rain came at the start, and that one is when rain did not come at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by splitting the cases. It depends on whether the land already got rain earlier in the season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If it rained enough before טבת, more rain in טבת does harm, so רב יהודה is right that a dry טבת is good. If it did not rain earlier, the land needs rain in טבת, so רב חסדא is right that a muddy טבת is good.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This is when rain came earlier,
that is when rain did not come earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא דַּאֲתָא מִיטְרָא מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction between רב יהודה and רב חסדא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (whether rain fell before טבת)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה and רב חסדא disagree about rain in טבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not disagree. A dry טבת is good after early rain, and a rainy טבת is good when no early rain fell.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether rain in טבת is good depends on the earlier rains: dry is better if it already rained, wet is better if it did not.

steps.title: Rain on part of a country is not the curse of closing the heavens
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that if rain falls on one part of a country but not another, it does not count as the curse of "וְעָצַר".
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: Rain that fell on part of a country, and did not fall on another part of the country, does not count as "and He will close up the heavens."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching of רב חסדא about rain. If only some areas get rain, that is not the punishment of "וְעָצַר" (closing the heavens).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curse in קריאת שמע, "וְעָצַר אֶת הַשָּׁמַיִם", means the heavens are shut and no rain comes. רב חסדא says partial rain is not that curse, since rain is still falling in the land. This is the rule the גמרא will now test.

keyTerms.meaning: part of a country or region
"and He will close up" the heavens, the curse of no rain (from קריאת שמע)
they do not count as, they are not included in

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
Rain that fell on part of a country
and did not fall on another part of the country
does not count as "and He will close up" the heavens.
phrases.notes: Refers to the curse in דברים 11:17.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching of רב חסדא defining when "וְעָצַר" does not apply, continuing his rulings in steps 16-17. It comes right after the טבת discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain on only part of a country is not the curse of "וְעָצַר".

steps.title: A פסוק in עמוס says rain on one city and not another is a curse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from a פסוק in עמוס. רב explains that partial rain is a curse for both areas.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But it is written: "And I also withheld the rain from you, when there were still three months until the harvest. I caused rain on one city, and on another city I did not cause rain. One piece of land was rained upon, etc." And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Both are a curse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב חסדא's rule. A נביא describes rain on one city and not on another as a punishment, and רב says both areas are cursed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said partial rain is not a curse. But the פסוק in עמוס lists partial rain as one of ה׳'s punishments. רב even says the city that did get rain is also cursed. That seems to contradict רב חסדא directly.

keyTerms.meaning: a piece or field of land

steps.confusionAlert: Do not miss the surprise in רב's statement. It is not only the dry city that is cursed. The city that got rain is cursed too. The next step explains why.

phrases.english: Is that so?
But isn't it written: "And I also
withheld the rain from you
when there were still three months until the harvest
and I caused rain on one city
and on another city I did not cause rain
one piece of land was rained upon, etc."
And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Both are for a curse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's rule from step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that partial rain is not a curse
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק and רב's reading treat partial rain as a curse for both the rainy area and the dry area. That contradicts רב חסדא.

steps.title: Too much rain is a curse, but the right amount is not
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק means a case where too much rain fell on one area. רב חסדא means the right amount fell there.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This (the פסוק) is where too much rain came. That (רב חסדא) is where rain came as much as was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by splitting the cases. A flood of rain on one area is a curse, but normal rain on one area is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why רב said the rainy city is also cursed: it got so much rain that it was damaged. רב חסדא is talking about a region that got the proper amount. That region is blessed, even though another region stayed dry.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this is where too much rain came,
that is where it came as much as was needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא from step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases (too much rain vs. the right amount)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Partial rain is always a curse, as the פסוק says.
steps.terutzMaskana: Partial rain is a curse only when the rainy area gets too much. A proper amount on one area is not a curse.

steps.title: The word for rained upon hints at flooding
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי supports the answer: the word "תִּמָּטֵר" means the area becomes a place full of rain, meaning flooded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The wording is also precise, as it is written "תִּמָּטֵר", which means it will be a place of rain. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support for the answer from the exact wording of the פסוק. The גמרא accepts it with "שמע מינה".
steps.deeperAnalysis: "תִּמָּטֵר" is read as "it will become a place of rain," meaning soaked and flooded. That shows the פסוק is talking about too much rain, just as the answer said. So the פסוק does not contradict רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: the wording is also precise (support from exact language)
a place of rain, flooded land

steps.whatToRemember: Rain on only part of the country is a curse only when that part is flooded. The right amount of rain in one area is not "וְעָצַר".

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: The wording is also precise,
as it is written: "was rained upon"
meaning it will be a place of rain (flooded).
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the תירוץ of step 28 from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the פסוק refers to too much rain
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word "תִּמָּטֵר" in עמוס 4:7, read as "a place of rain"
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The curse in עמוס is about flooding. רב חסדא's rule about a normal amount of partial rain stands.

steps.title: When we begin to bless over rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו teaches that we say the ברכה on rain once enough rain falls that "the groom goes out to meet the bride".
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: From when do we say a ברכה on rain? From when the groom goes out to meet the bride.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: the ברכה on rain. רבי אבהו gives a picture to show how much rain must fall first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "groom" is the falling raindrops and the "bride" is the water already on the ground. Once puddles form and the drops splash up to meet them, the rain is real and worth a ברכה. A few light drops are not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: a groom toward a bride, the image of raindrops meeting puddles

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about weddings. It is a picture: falling drops (groom) splash into puddles on the ground (bride).

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
From when do we say a blessing on rain?
From when the groom goes out to meet the bride.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מֵאֵימָתַי מְבָרְכִין עַל הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about rain: the ברכה said over it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We say the ברכה on rain once enough has fallen to form puddles that the drops splash into.

steps.title: What blessing is said over rain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words of the ברכה on rain are.
steps.simpleTranslation: What ברכה does one say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to set up the next step. We know when to bless; now we want the actual words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו told us the timing but not the text. This question opens the way for the opinions of רב and רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: What blessing does one say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on רבי אבהו's teaching by asking for the text of the ברכה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact words of the ברכה on rain

steps.title: Thanking God for every single drop
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב gives the text: "We thank You, ה׳ our God, for every drop You brought down for us."
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: "We thank You, ה׳ our God, for each and every drop that You brought down for us."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with רב's text of the ברכה. It is a short thank-you for each drop of rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברכה is a הודאה (thanksgiving), not a request. Saying "each and every drop" shows thanks for every bit of rain, not just for rain in general.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
"We thank You, ה׳ our God,

phrases.aramaic: עַל כׇּל טִפָּה וְטִפָּה שֶׁהוֹרַדְתָּ לָנוּ״.
phrases.english: for each and every drop that You brought down for us."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מוֹדִים אֲנַחְנוּ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה begins "מודים אנחנו לך ה׳ אלהינו על כל טפה וטפה שהורדת לנו".

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's longer ending to the blessing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן ends the ברכה with words like נשמת: "If our mouth were full of song like the sea...", ending "ברוך רוב ההודאות".
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן finishes it like this: "If our mouth were full of song like the sea, and our tongue full of joyful song like the many waves, etc.", until "May Your mercy not leave us, ה׳ our God, and it has not left us. Blessed is [the One of] many thanks."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבי יוחנן's ending to רב's ברכה. It is a long praise, like the נשמת we say on שבת morning, and it ends with a closing ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not argue with רב. He adds an ending to the same ברכה. The idea is that even with endless song we could never thank ה׳ enough for rain, so the ברכה ends by calling Him the One worthy of many thanks.

keyTerms.meaning: if our mouth were full of song like the sea (from נשמת)
blessed is the One of many thanks, the closing ברכה

steps.whatToRemember: The ברכה on rain is said once there are puddles (רבי אבהו). It opens "מודים אנחנו לך... על כל טפה וטפה" (רב), and רבי יוחנן adds the נשמת-style ending, "ברוך רוב ההודאות".
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that rain was seen as a huge gift that deserves full thanksgiving, like the praise we say on שבת.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan concludes it like this:
"If our mouth were full of song like the sea
and our tongue with joyful song like its many waves, etc."
until: "May Your mercy not leave us, ה׳ our God,
and it has not left us.
Blessed is [the One of] many thanks."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a closing to רב's ברכה from step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברכה continues with the נשמת text and ends "ברוך רוב ההודאות".

steps.title: Why say 'most of the thanks' instead of 'all of the thanks'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ending "רוב ההודאות". It sounds as if ה׳ deserves only most of our thanks and not all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does the ברכה say "most of the thanks" and not "all of the thanks"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is questioning the last words of רבי יוחנן's ברכה from the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "רוב" means "most" or "the majority". Saying ה׳ is blessed with "most" of the thanks seems to suggest that some thanks belongs elsewhere. The גמרא expects the wording to be "כל ההודאות", meaning all the thanks.

phrases.english: "Most of the thanksgivings" and not "all the thanksgivings"?
phrases.notes: The question is quoting the ending of רבי יוחנן's ברכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the closing words of רבי יוחנן's ברכה
steps.kashyaTarget: The ending "ברוך רוב ההודאות" in רבי יוחנן's text
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: "רוב" (most) seems to limit how much thanks ה׳ deserves. The wording should be "כל" (all).

steps.title: רבא changes the wording to 'God of thanksgivings'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers by changing the text. Say "אל ההודאות", God of thanksgivings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Say instead "God of thanksgivings."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question by correcting the wording of the ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not defend the word "רוב". He replaces the phrase with "אל ההודאות". This wording calls ה׳ the God of all thanks and has no hint of a limit, so the problem goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (instead); a word used to correct a text

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not explaining what "רוב" means. He is replacing the wording altogether.

phrases.english: Rava said: Say instead:
"God of thanksgivings."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 34
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ending is "רוב ההודאות", which sounds like ה׳ gets only most of the thanks.
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct ending is "אל ההודאות", which has no limiting word.

steps.title: רב פפא begins a practical ruling
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא opens with "הלכך" (therefore). He is starting a practical ruling based on the different versions of the ברכה. The ruling itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רב פפא is about to give a practical ruling, and the rest of his words appear on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "הלכך" signals a practical result drawn from what came before. Since there are different opinions about the wording, רב פפא is about to tell us how to say the ברכה in practice.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore,
phrases.notes: His statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the differing versions to set up a practical ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. רב פפא is opening a practical ruling about the ברכה's wording that continues on the next amud.
